questions.prompt: According to the Claude Code docs, what does the term agentic harness refer to?

options.text: The model weights that do the reasoning
options.explanation: The model reasons. The harness is the layer around it.

options.text: The layer around the model that provides the tools and manages its context
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI uses the word the same way: its harness runs the model and tool loop and keeps the session.

options.text: The sandbox where shell commands run
options.explanation: That is the environment. OpenAI's Agents API treats the harness and the environment as separate pieces.

questions.prompt: You want to embed an agent loop as a library in your own app. Which pair matches?

options.text: Claude Agent SDK and OpenAI Agents SDK
options.explanation: Right. Both run the loop inside your application.

options.text: Claude Managed Agents and OpenAI Agents API
options.explanation: Those are hosted: the vendor runs the loop for you.

options.text: Claude Client SDK and OpenAI Responses API
options.explanation: With these you write the loop yourself.

questions.prompt: A rule must hold on every tool call: never run `git push --force`. Where does it belong?

options.text: In the instruction file, in bold
options.explanation: The Claude Code docs say an instruction in CLAUDE.md is a request, not a guarantee.

options.text: In a hook that blocks the call
options.explanation: Right. A hook always fires on its event. If a rule must hold every time, make it a hook.

options.text: In a skill the agent can load
options.explanation: A skill is interpreted by the model, so the outcome can vary.
